nba_directive.reason_text: This client has a 2.99% rate that should never be touched via cash-out refi, but they ARE bleeding $48/month in PMI that builds zero equity — that's the concrete, immediate pain point to anchor the delay around while pinning a specific callback so the conversation doesn't go cold.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Lead with the PMI as found money, not a rate pitch
  - Name it directly: '$48/month in PMI on a conventional loan is money that disappears — it doesn't reduce your $205,076 balance by a single dollar'
  - At $48/mo, that's $576/year in pure waste — quantify how many months/years they've already paid it and what's left ahead if nothing changes
  - Do NOT mention touching their 2.99% rate — frame this entire conversation around eliminating PMI only

- Tie the PMI escape to their stated life goal
  - Ask directly: 'You mentioned wanting to revisit later — what's the goal behind that timing? Retirement, paying something off, a specific date?'
  - Once they name it, anchor the math: 'Every month we wait is another $48 that doesn't move you toward [their goal] — that's real dollars we can redirect'
  - Calculate (or coach the client to see) how many months remain until their balance naturally hits the LTV threshold where PMI drops — if that date is far out, the case for acting sooner gets stronger

- Honor the delay but make it concrete, not open-ended
  - Say: 'I completely respect the timing — I just want to make sure we're not leaving money on the table while we wait'
  - Pin a specific callback: 'Can we put 10 minutes on the calendar for [specific date]? I'll have the exact LTV number and PMI removal timeline ready so you can make a fully informed call'
  - Do not leave the follow-up as 'reach out when you're ready' — get a date and time confirmed in this text thread

- Carry the 'you can always refinance again later' reframe as a safety net
  - Remind them: 'Removing PMI now doesn't lock you into anything — if rates drop further down the road, you can still refinance then. This is just stopping the bleed in the meantime'
  - This neutralizes the 'I'll wait for better rates' objection without ever conceding that their 2.99% rate should be refinanced today

- Secure the micro-commitment before closing the text
  - Offer two options: 'Want me to run the exact LTV and PMI removal timeline now, or save it for our call on [proposed date]?'
  - Either answer moves the loan forward — one gets you data to send, the other locks the callback
